messages.subject: Model Residuals help
parts:
Dear Chris Watson,

Thank you so much for sharing this toolbox!

I am trying to reproduce cortical thickness pipeline you explained in manual pdf file just for 14 subjects. I've encountered many errors during process but I was lucky enough to spot my mistakes and correct them, until "model residuals" step. Whenever I input;


all.dat.resids <- get.resid(all.dat.tidy, covars, exclude='Group')


I get following error;


Error in parse(text = x) : <text>:2:0: unexpected end of input
1: value ~  ##
   ^




I think there is a problem with my covars.csv file but it worked until now so I am confused. I am attaching the file so maybe you want to check it.

I never used R statistics package before so maybe my question is out of scope of your toolbox, sorry.

Best regards
Ozgun Ozalay

So, I recommend removing the first column, thus leaving only "Group" and "Study.ID", and trying again. Let me know if any more errors occur.

Chris

messages.author: 28bb28f8fe8898a5
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Model Residuals help
parts:
Ah, I see the problem now. Since you are not adjusting for any covariates, there is no linear model that can be applied, and therefore no residuals to obtain. In this case, you can skip Chapter 4.3 of the User Guide and go straight to Chapter 4.5. The code to apply will be in the second gray box of that section (that starts with "# Correlate raw thickness"). Since you have a single group, the code you want would be:

kNumSubjs <- nrow(covars)
corrs <- lapply(densities, function(x) corr.matrix(lhrh, density=x))

Then I think you should be able to follow the remainder of the User Guide as-is.

Let me know if that works,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Model Residuals help
parts:
Hi Ozgun, I am glad you were able to get things working.

Regarding the "g.L" and plotting, I did not include all of the code that goes into creating that graph object. This is because it is generally quite a hassle, and I think it is much easier to use "plot_brainGraph_gui"; then, if you would like to plot the left hemisphere only, you can simply select the appropriate GUI option.

However, for your information, below will be the code to create the single-hemisphere graph:
----
memb.hemi <- which(V(g[[1]][[N]])$hemi == 'L')
g.sub <- induced.subgraph(g[[1]][[N]], memb.hemi)
for (att in graph_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_graph_attr(g.sub, att)
for (att in vertex_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_vertex_attr(g.sub, att)
for (att in edge_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_edge_attr(g.sub, att)
V(g.sub)$name <- V(g[[1]][[N]])$name[memb.hemi]
V(g.sub)$hemi <- V(g[[1]][[N]])$hemi[memb.hemi]
g.L <- graph.intersection(g[[1]][[N]], g.sub, keep.all.vertices=F)

atlas.dt <- eval(parse(text=data(list=atlas)))
layout.g.L <- matrix(c(-atlas.dt[memb.hemi, y.mni],
                       atlas.dt[memb.hemi, z.mni]),
                   ncol=2, byrow=F)
xlim.g.L <- c(-85, 110)
ylim.g.L <- c(-85, 125)

# Plot with vertex and edge colors representing communities, vertex size proportional to "degree", and edge width proportional to betweenness
plot_brainGraph_mni('sagittal', slice=30, hemi='left')
plot_brainGraph(g.L, vertex.label=NA, vertex.size=100*V(g.L)$degree,
         xlim=xlim.g.L, ylim=ylim.g.L, layout=layout.g.L,
         vertex.color=V(g.L)$color.comm, edge.color=E(g.L)$color.comm,
         edge.width=log1p(E(g.L)$btwn))


Let me know if you have other questions,
Chris

On Tuesday, May 10, 2016 at 10:43:26 PM UTC+9, Chris Watson wrote:
Hi Ozgun, I am glad you were able to get things working.

Regarding the "g.L" and plotting, I did not include all of the code that goes into creating that graph object. This is because it is generally quite a hassle, and I think it is much easier to use "plot_brainGraph_gui"; then, if you would like to plot the left hemisphere only, you can simply select the appropriate GUI option.

However, for your information, below will be the code to create the single-hemisphere graph:
----
memb.hemi <- which(V(g[[1]][[N]])$hemi == 'L')
g.sub <- induced.subgraph(g[[1]][[N]], memb.hemi)
for (att in graph_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_graph_attr(g.sub, att)
for (att in vertex_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_vertex_attr(g.sub, att)
for (att in edge_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_edge_attr(g.sub, att)
V(g.sub)$name <- V(g[[1]][[N]])$name[memb.hemi]
V(g.sub)$hemi <- V(g[[1]][[N]])$hemi[memb.hemi]
g.L <- graph.intersection(g[[1]][[N]], g.sub, keep.all.vertices=F)

atlas.dt <- eval(parse(text=data(list=atlas)))
layout.g.L <- matrix(c(-atlas.dt[memb.hemi, y.mni],
                       atlas.dt[memb.hemi, z.mni]),
                   ncol=2, byrow=F)
xlim.g.L <- c(-85, 110)
ylim.g.L <- c(-85, 125)

# Plot with vertex and edge colors representing communities, vertex size proportional to "degree", and edge width proportional to betweenness
plot_brainGraph_mni('sagittal', slice=30, hemi='left')
plot_brainGraph(g.L, vertex.label=NA, vertex.size=100*V(g.L)$degree,
         xlim=xlim.g.L, ylim=ylim.g.L, layout=layout.g.L,
         vertex.color=V(g.L)$color.comm, edge.color=E(g.L)$color.comm,
         edge.width=log1p(E(g.L)$btwn))


Let me know if you have other questions,
Chris

On Tuesday, May 10, 2016 at 10:43:26 PM UTC+9, Chris Watson wrote:
Hi Ozgun, I am glad you were able to get things working.

Regarding the "g.L" and plotting, I did not include all of the code that goes into creating that graph object. This is because it is generally quite a hassle, and I think it is much easier to use "plot_brainGraph_gui"; then, if you would like to plot the left hemisphere only, you can simply select the appropriate GUI option.

However, for your information, below will be the code to create the single-hemisphere graph:
----
memb.hemi <- which(V(g[[1]][[N]])$hemi == 'L')
g.sub <- induced.subgraph(g[[1]][[N]], memb.hemi)
for (att in graph_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_graph_attr(g.sub, att)
for (att in vertex_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_vertex_attr(g.sub, att)
for (att in edge_attr_names(g.sub)) g.sub <- delete_edge_attr(g.sub, att)
V(g.sub)$name <- V(g[[1]][[N]])$name[memb.hemi]
V(g.sub)$hemi <- V(g[[1]][[N]])$hemi[memb.hemi]
g.L <- graph.intersection(g[[1]][[N]], g.sub, keep.all.vertices=F)

atlas.dt <- eval(parse(text=data(list=atlas)))
layout.g.L <- matrix(c(-atlas.dt[memb.hemi, y.mni],
                       atlas.dt[memb.hemi, z.mni]),
                   ncol=2, byrow=F)
xlim.g.L <- c(-85, 110)
ylim.g.L <- c(-85, 125)

# Plot with vertex and edge colors representing communities, vertex size proportional to "degree", and edge width proportional to betweenness
plot_brainGraph_mni('sagittal', slice=30, hemi='left')
plot_brainGraph(g.L, vertex.label=NA, vertex.size=100*V(g.L)$degree,
         xlim=xlim.g.L, ylim=ylim.g.L, layout=layout.g.L,
         vertex.color=V(g.L)$color.comm, edge.color=E(g.L)$color.comm,
         edge.width=log1p(E(g.L)$btwn))


Let me know if you have other questions,
Chris
